title: Temple of Hercules Victor
visualBrief: Temple of Hercules Victor present-day medium-fi exterior: nineteen individually mapped fluted Corinthian shafts and the isolated surviving twentieth base, low circular stepped podium and east entrance steps, round brick/marble cella with a closed recessed arched door, broad shallow tiled conical roof with visible timber underside and small summit cap. Include simplified capital leaf/corner silhouettes and selected protective shaft bands. No lost ancient entablature or original roof is reconstructed. Neighboring Portunus, churches, modern streets and gardens stay independent.

sourceFacts.horizontalBasis: Q576929/way251342364 fixes the circular temple. Eleven pinned standard PMTiles records supply the main footprint, podium, nineteen separate standing shaft polygons in one feature, isolated base, C-shaped cella, roof, roof cap and four east stair parts. The open east sector of the mapped cella and stair projection resolve the entrance facing east, independently of the circle bounding-box axis. Raw+X east/+Z south at runtime heading0; each mapped shaft keeps its individual center.
sourceFacts.architecturalHeights: Standard-map parts give podium0.8m, nineteen shaft tops8m, cella8.5m, roof8–10m and cap10.5m above the lower datum. The model follows this approximate envelope: fluted shaft1.0–7.0m, Corinthian crown7.0–8.0m, timber support8.0–8.25m and shallow roof8.25–10.15m. Ordinary frontal and capital pictures guide the present roof, leaf masses, flute/drum/band treatment, brick upper cella and pale lower panels. Exact carvings, repairs, tie bands, door joinery and surveyed heights are not claimed.
